title: The standard library
description:
Use modules from the standard library (lesson 3.04) instead of writing everything yourself:

```python
def roll_dice(count, sides, seed): ...     # a list of count rolls from 1 to sides, using random.Random(seed)
def summary(values): ...                   # (mean, median, mode) using the statistics module
def days_between(start, end): ...          # days from start to end, dates written "YYYY-MM-DD", using datetime
def is_prime(n): ...                       # True for primes; use math.isqrt for the square root
```

`random.Random(seed)` makes a generator that always produces the same sequence for the same seed; call its `randint(1, sides)` once per roll.
hints: The `statistics` module has `mean`, `median` and `mode` functions, each taking a list.

`from datetime import date`, then `date.fromisoformat("2026-01-01")` turns text in the YYYY-MM-DD form into a date (lesson 6.03 covers dates in depth). Subtracting two `date` objects gives a `timedelta`, whose `.days` is the answer.
`math.isqrt(n)` is the whole-number square root. A number is prime if no `d` from 2 up to that root divides it (`n % d == 0`); numbers below 2 are not prime.
